content.title: U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Seen Settling Above 4% For Now
content.summary: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield "seems content at above 4% for now," ING's Padhraic Garvey and Benjamin Schroeder said in a note.  U.S. Treasury yields closed lower on Tuesday but the falls were small.  U.S. Treasury yields edged lower, with the 10-year yield down 1.9 basis points at 4.070%, according to Tradeweb data.

content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Decline After Lowered Borrowing Estimate
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields were falling in early trade, with U.S. quarterly borrowing in focus.  The U.S. Treasury lowered the fourth-quarter borrowing estimate by $21 billion to $569 billion, "primarily due to the higher beginning-of-quarter cash balance, partially offset by lower projected net cash flows," it said.  The 10-year Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.086%, while the 30-year yield was down 2.1 basis points at 4.668%, according to Tradeweb.
